policy.intent: Staging area for bugs surfaced during pilot / benchmark runs.
policy.review_cycle_cadence: At every phase boundary (pre-task / pre-full-benchmark / pre-paper-submission).
rules: Every bug must have a reproducer.
Bugs closed 'fixed-shipped' must include verifying evidence.

bugs.title: S2 stop-rule pre-empts S3 when both fire at same iter
bugs.discovered_during: smoke test M0/M1/M2/M3 with IR-schema protocol
bugs.evidence: run_benchmark_v0.2.py stop-rule block: S1>S2>S3 ordering caused S2 to fire when ir_t1==ir_current even if Success(C)=True, under-reporting success_at_K.
bugs.fix_committed_in: run_benchmark_v0.2.py:1090-1102 — reordered to S1>S3>S2. Verified: re_read_pilot_results.py shows S3 now fires correctly when success=True.

bugs.title: Protocol §2.2 'import FreeCAD' pre-flight check unrealisable but solver path works
bugs.evidence: freecad_sketcher env lacks 'FreeCAD' module (uppercase) but has 'freecad' shim. solver_runner works from cad_subproject1 env in-process.

bugs.title: run_benchmark_v0.2 collapses (sample_id, negative_id) pair — out_dir clash
bugs.evidence: run_one_sample used sample_id only for out_dir; multiple negs per sample overwrote each other; aggregate() KeyError.
bugs.fix_committed_in: run_benchmark_v0.2.py: parse_sample_arg() + load_initial_ir() + run_benchmark(samples: list[tuple]) + aggregate error-filter. Verified: 18/18 parseable run_result.json per method, 0 errors.

bugs.title: _pipeline_valid enum mismatch: adaptor writes 'pass', validator compares 'success'
bugs.evidence: adapter_report.json has step_export_status='pass'; _pipeline_valid compared == 'success'. All 72 pilot runs showed pipeline_valid=False despite genuine STEP export success.
bugs.fix_committed_in: run_benchmark_v0.2.py: _is_truthy_status() helper accepting {'success','pass','ok','true'}; _pipeline_valid rewritten. Verified by re_read_pilot_results.py: pipeline_valid now True where adapter succeeded.

bugs.title: task5 perturbation battery + iter_0 always-Success means agent is NEVER exercised; pipeline_valid=True reveals pilot perturbation battery is too weak
bugs.discovered_during: Pilot re-read after B-001 + B-004 fix; per-method discrimination collapsed to identical 55.6%
bugs.evidence: After B-001 + B-004 fixes, re_read_pilot_results.py shows all 4 methods × 18 samples have P=True,S=True,K=True at iter_0 → S3 fires immediately → agent never called → Success@1=Success@3 for all methods. The perturbed IR from task5 battery passes KQP tolerance without repair. Methods are indistinguishable because the agent is never called.
bugs.reproducer: python experiments/pilot/re_read_pilot_results.py → inspect iter_records_summary: every iter_0 = success=True, stop_reason=stop_S3_success_at_iter_1.
bugs.fix_proposal: (a) Increase perturbation scale (E1/E2 ×2.0 instead of ×1.5); (b) tighten KQP tolerance in frozen instances; (c) add new perturbation operators that break KQP more aggressively. ~4-6 hours.
bugs.risk_if_kept: Cannot measure M0≠M1≠M2≠M3 — the ablation's core proposition is untestable on this battery. §6.2 critical check (M0≠M2 on KQP-visible stratum) fails because both are identical.
bugs.obsolescence_reason: Re-read (2026-07-16 21:30) shows the actual blocker is not perturbation strength — it's that 7/8 failures are sketch_annulus samples where the FreeCAD solver_runner returns solve_status='conflicting' + exception='no lines in sketch' because the shim doesn't add concentric constraints for annulus shapes. Agent cannot fix this (it can only change params, not op_type). B-005 was a symptom misdiagnosis; the real bug is B-006 (solver_runner annulus translation).

bugs.title: Pilot perturbation battery is dominated by Design-Plan self-diagnosis; KQP feedback channel is structurally redundant
bugs.evidence: All 7 LLM-repaired successes emit the exact KQP-feedback-expected value, but M0's [FEEDBACK] block contains NO KQP channel — only the pipeline block. The expected value (e.g., 130.0 mm) appears 3 times in the M0 prompt, all in the [DESIGN PLAN] block: extrude.distance_total.value=130.0, dimensions.extrude_distance.value=130.0, and q_span_w: expected=130.0 (KQP query list embedded in DesignPlan.validation_intents). The LLM is reading the Design Plan, NOT the KQP feedback. M0 ≡ M2 ≡ M3 across the pilot because all methods have equal access to the Design Plan; the KQP feedback channel is unused for parameter-value selection on this battery.
bugs.reproducer: Open M0 agent_request.json for any of the 7 repaired successes; observe that the [FEEDBACK] block contains only the pipeline sub-block (no kqp sub-block) and the KQP expected value is absent from [FEEDBACK] but present in [DESIGN PLAN].
bugs.fix_proposal: Pilot battery is not a true feedback ablation. To test feedback value, perturbations must exceed the Design Plan's information content: (a) introduce perturbations that the DP cannot directly specify (e.g., a different extrude direction; perturbed tolerance); (b) test cases where the LLM has to reconcile conflicting DP fields; (c) samples with multi-step repairs where one step uses DP and another uses feedback. Otherwise M0 ≡ M2 ≡ M3 ≡ M1 is a structural property, not a feedback-value measurement.
bugs.risk_if_kept: The current pilot cannot answer the §3.1 RQ1/RQ2/RQ3 (feedback value). All 4 methods are demonstrably equivalent on this battery. The ablation can only measure 'feedback value on perturbations that exceed DP knowledge', which requires perturbation redesign.

bugs.title: solver_runner returns solve_status='conflicting' for sketch_annulus shapes (no concentric constraints generated)
bugs.discovered_during: Pilot failure analysis: 7/8 failed samples are sketch_annulus
bugs.evidence: All 7 sketch_annulus samples in the pilot return solver_feedback.json with: solve_status='conflicting', exception='no lines in sketch', flags.has_solver_error=True, dof=0. The solver_runner.py translates sketch_annulus (2 concentric circles) into FreeCAD geometry but doesn't add Concentric/Equal constraints, so FreeCAD sees two unconstrained circles. Result: SolverValid=False → §4.2 conjunction fails → sample is unfixable regardless of method/agent.
bugs.reproducer: Run solver_runner on any annulus IR; observe solve_status='conflicting' + exception='no lines in sketch'. Sample list: 102410_f9877a7b_0000/neg_01, /neg_02; 102410_f9877a7b_0012/neg_01, /neg_02; 103284_e25015aa_0003/neg_03; 106323_77f22d29_0004/neg_01; 107668_cf76b132_0001/neg_02.
bugs.fix_proposal: (1) Added CircleSpec dataclass + Part.Circle support in probe_lib.build_sketch(). (2) Added 'Concentric' constraint type (implemented as Coincident on circle centres pos=3 since this FreeCAD build's Sketcher.Constraint doesn't accept 'Concentric' name in its binding). (3) Added 'Radius' constraint type (fixed pre-existing param-order bug). (4) history_parser now emits SketchCircle as CircleSpec + auto-injects Concentric + Radius for annulus shapes (2+ circles without explicit F360 constraints). (5) solver_runner now uses build_sketch's num_circles (not FreeCAD's GeometryCount which counts lines only).
bugs.risk_if_kept: 7/18 pilot samples (and likely ~25-40% of full 104-sample benchmark) are structurally unfixable by the current SolverRunner. The §4.2 Success conjunction always fails on these because SolverValid=False. Cannot distinguish M0 from M1 from M2 from M3 on annulus samples. Pilot cannot test the ablation on these.
bugs.decider: execution agent (per Step 1 of user-approved 3-step plan)
bugs.fix_committed_in: Freecadsolver_feedback/api_probe/probe_lib.py (CircleSpec, Part.Circle with Vector, Concentric via Coincident, Radius with target_geo+params[0]); Freecadsolver_feedback/core/history_parser.py (SketchCircle branch, ConcentricConstraint + RadiusConstraint handlers, auto-inject Concentric+Radius for 2+ circles); Freecadsolver_feedback/core/solver_runner.py (no-geometry check uses lines AND circles, num_circles from build_sketch). Verified: 7/7 annulus samples now solver_valid=True (rc=0, status=success, dof=2, under_constrained).

bugs.title: Reconstruction Engine executor ignores reference_plane u_direction/v_direction — EX1/EX2 perturbations invisible at IR layer
bugs.discovered_during: EX1/EX2 operator implementation + behavioral equivalence check (plan §6.1)
bugs.evidence: Reconstruction Engine compiler reads plane.{origin, u_direction, v_direction, normal} into recipe["plane"], but the generated code only uses recipe["plane"]["normal"] to flip the sign of ext (if nz<0). It does NOT use u_direction / v_direction to rotate the cadquery Workplane. EX1/EX2 perturbed histories have u_direction and v_direction swapped, but the resulting STEP has the SAME bbox as the clean STEP (verified: 100877_ac1e5a17_0001 — clean bbox (279.4, 215.9, 1.5875), EX1 bbox (279.4, 215.9, 1.5875) IDENTICAL; KQP detection rate 0/3).
bugs.reproducer: Apply op_EX1_sketch_plane_swap on 100877_ac1e5a17_0001; run Reconstruction Engine; compare bbox of clean vs perturbed STEP. The two are identical.
bugs.fix_proposal: Modify executor to (a) build the cadquery Workplane on the plane defined by plane.origin + plane.u_direction + plane.v_direction + plane.normal (i.e., construct a custom plane via cadquery.Plane); (b) extrude along plane.normal not world Z.  ~2-4 hours depending on test infrastructure.
bugs.risk_if_kept: None — the executor does not need fixing. Restore from backup: cp reconstruction_engine/executor_v0.1_FROZEN.py reconstruction_engine/executor.py and cp reconstruction_engine/compiler_v0.1_FROZEN.py reconstruction_engine/compiler.py. The 50 clean samples will continue to work.
bugs.misdiagnosis_note: The executor IS NOT broken. It correctly uses cq.Workplane(WORKPLANE) and EX1/EX2 perturbations DO change the body bbox in 3D. The real blocker is in the KQP layer (see B-009): the best-match strategy in query_dispatcher.py masks world-axis reorders. EX1 reorders the body bbox between world axes (e.g. XY to XZ produces a 3D bbox where the rectangle is on XZ instead of XY), but KQP picks the world axis closest to the expected value, so all 3 queries still pass.
bugs.reclassification_note: Originally B-008 was filed on the hypothesis that the executor (reconstruction_engine/executor.py) does not honor u_dir/v_dir. After verification, the executor IS correct (it uses cq.Workplane(WORKPLANE) which DOES produce a different body bbox for EX1/EX2). The real issue is the KQP layer (see B-009). Restored from backup.

bugs.title: KQP best-match strategy masks world-axis bbox reorders (EX1/EX2 perturbations are undetectable at KQP layer)
bugs.evidence: EX1 perturbation on sample 100877_ac1e5a17_0001 (XY plane) successfully swaps plane to XZ. Reconstruction Engine correctly generates code with NORMAL=(0,1,0), WORKPLANE=XZ. Body bbox changes from (279.4, 215.9, 1.5875) (XY-extrude-Z) to (279.4, 1.5875, 215.9) (XZ-extrude-Y), which is a different world-axis assignment of the same SET of values. KQP query_dispatcher.py:60-83 (best-match strategy) for axis-aligned frames maps each query (u/v/w) to the world axis with the closest span, so all 3 queries (u=279.4, v=215.9, w=1.5875) still pass. KQP detection rate 0/3 for EX1.
bugs.reproducer: Apply op_EX1_sketch_plane_swap on 100877_ac1e5a17_0001; run Reconstruction Engine; compute KQP. All 3 bbox queries return status=pass despite body in different orientation.
bugs.fix_proposal: Modify kqp/runner/query_dispatcher.py: replace best-match with frame-axis projection (use get_bbox_size_along_frame_axis) for ALL queries, not just rotated frames. This makes the queries strictly aligned with the u/v/w frame defined in the KQP instance, so a plane swap in the IR translates to a query failure. Risk: changes the behavior of the existing 50 clean samples (where the frame IS already aligned with the world); needs verification that best-match was only useful as a safety net for rotated frames and is not the primary correctness path.
bugs.reclassification_note: B-009 was filed on the hypothesis that the KQP best-match strategy was masking world-axis reorders. After 2 fix attempts (frame-only and hybrid), the root cause was found to be deeper: EX1 (plane swap) and EX2 (axis flip within plane) produce bodies whose bbox is a *permutation* of the original body bbox. KQP best-match correctly picks the closest world span, and frame-axis projection gives a result that mismatches expected — but the mismatch is between the *expected* value (sourced from the design plan) and the *frame-axis projected* value. The design plan u/v/w EXPECTED values match the original body frame. The body bbox has the same SET of values regardless of frame orientation. Hence: the EX perturbation is a fundamental identity-preserving reorder of the bbox SET, and is undetectable by ANY KQP method that compares per-axis spans to expected per-axis values. A different perturbation type (one that changes the SET, not just the order) is needed. Restored kqp/runner/query_dispatcher.py from backup at experiments/kqp/runner/query_dispatcher_v0.1_FROZEN.py.

bugs.title: EX1 plane-swap produces bodies whose bbox values match the DP expected values for some samples (frame u/v in DP equals pre-EX1 body orientation, not post)
bugs.discovered_during: Full EX battery re-verification after B-010 fix
bugs.evidence: After B-010 + frame-only, EX1 is detected in 10/29 samples (34%) at the sample level, 20/87 (23%) at the bbox-query level. EX2 detects 23/28 (82%) samples, 61/84 (72.6%) queries. The 19 EX1 samples not detected have the property that the design plan's expected_u value is small enough that the frame-axis projection still produces a value within tolerance — e.g., the body is square (u==v in the original orientation) and the swap does not change which world axis has the matching span. EX2 is more reliably detected because it changes a value within the same plane, which the dispatcher does not mask with the best-match tolerance.
bugs.reproducer: Apply EX1 to sample 100877 (279.4 x 215.9 rect on XY plane, EX1 swaps to XZ). New bbox is (279.4, 1.588, 215.9). The DP expected_u=279.4 matches world X (which equals 279.4 post-EX1), so q_bbox_u passes. q_bbox_v expected=215.9 fails (world Y is 1.588, not 215.9). q_bbox_w expected=1.5875 fails (world Z is 215.9, not 1.588). For other samples where the body is square (e.g., 19x19) the swap is invisible to the bbox-value comparison.
bugs.fix_proposal: Either (i) modify EX1 to also re-derive the DP's expected_u and expected_v from the perturbed body (e.g., swap the values to match the new orientation), OR (ii) for EX1, only generate perturbations on non-square body samples, OR (iii) re-derive the DP expected values for the perturbed body to give the post-EX1 KQP instance. The cleanest fix is (i): use a "synthesized" KQP instance for the EX1 perturbed sample where the expected values are flipped to match the new body orientation. This requires changes in both the EX1 operator and the KQP instance generation.
bugs.risk_if_kept: C-path filter (non-square profiles) raised EX1 sample-level detection from 10/29 (34%) to 4/18 (22%) of NON-SQUARE samples. EX1 detection remains below 80% threshold. Root cause: even for non-square bodies, the 3D bbox SET can be the same after plane swap when the 2D rect spans and the extrude are close to each other. The plan cross-stage rule R5 says: if the EX layer shows M0 ≈ M2, stop and escalate. M0/M2 pre-validation on EX battery is the next gate.
bugs.fix_committed_in: task5_negative_perturbation/perturbation/sampler_ex.py: added is_non_square_profile() guard that filters EX1 to samples where length_u ≠ width_v (28 square samples excluded from EX1 out of 46).
